cells.tense: Right now you keep several things open and pick the live ones without hurry.
cells.ask: Take one thing you have left open a while. Set a day this week to give it a shape or put it down. Both finishes count.
cells.core:
You keep a lot open and you do it well. Nothing has come up yet and you are not forcing any of it. Things get your care while they are small and unproven, and you can also set down what is spent without a scene and turn toward what is still growing. That looseness is the hard part and you have it.

What this balance asks in return is a turn of its own. Every open thing takes upkeep, and some of what you keep is kept from habit rather than because it is alive. Give the thing actually growing a little more than the ones held just in case. And when you put a date or a name on one of them, that moment is what all the waiting was for.
cells.sheetLine: You keep things open and you can let the spent ones go.
cells.verb: keeping what is ripe and turning what is spent back under

cells.tense: You are living past an ending that has not arrived, bracing like it already happened.
cells.ask: Name one ending you are sure is coming. Say it once, out loud, to someone who will just listen, and leave it there.
cells.core:
You are running an outcome ahead of itself. The ending is still ahead and already settled in how you hold it — the plan made for the other person, the goodbye half-practiced, the answer given before the question. Whoever is across from you can feel a loss that has not happened, and it wears you down.

What you brace against may not land in the form you drew it. Endings here are what has simply run its course, and they do not need your help finishing early. Say the one you are sure about, out loud, to a person who will stay while you do. Nothing else. The managing can wait until there is something to manage.
cells.sheetLine: You are finishing something early that is still here.

cells.tense: Nothing here has started or ended, and you are waiting on a signal that is not coming.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you want and take a small step toward it today, before the timing feels right.
cells.core:
You are sitting with everything unstarted. Nothing is in the ground, and the waiting has started to look like patience from outside. Nothing has run its course, nothing has been picked, and the days pass without much marking them. It does not take a catastrophe to land here — it takes a stretch of ordinary weeks.

The missing piece is not a sign. It is starting something on a day that feels like nothing special, without a guarantee it will work. One step toward one thing you actually want, not the thing on the list that everyone expects. Small is fine. Starting makes the next step available, and moving has a way of showing you what was ripe.
cells.sheetLine: Nothing is planted and nothing is picked, and you call it patience.

cells.tense: You are deciding what ends and what keeps going here, and you talk as if it were not you.
cells.ask: Take one thing you have been calling the situation or the timing. Say out loud, once, that you decided it.
cells.core:
You are the one who knows when something is done. You feel it before it shows, and you stop feeding one thing or keep another alive because you can tell it is not finished. Your account has these endings arriving on their own, like they were not a choice. But they land when you let them land, and what gets kept has your hand on it the whole time.

If you are the one who says when a thing is over, then you are also the one who says what gets made next. That is the same hand. It would be worth owning out loud before the next round starts, because a decision you have not claimed can be given away without your catching it.
cells.sheetLine: You decide what ends here. Your account leaves you out of it.
